notes: No kb/Work note owns the fix (none found for the phrase order at 85). §1985:VII.4.4.2 prints READ file-name-1 [ NEXT ] RECORD [ INTO identifier-1 ], then [ AT END imperative-statement-1 ], then [ NOT AT END imperative-statement-2 ], then [ END-READ ]. Implemented at 85: the superset rule readStatement keeps NEXT, RECORD and INTO in the printed sequence (INTO before RECORD, RECORD twice and INTO after the phrases are COBOL2269), the conditionalPhrases loop takes each phrase once, with an imperative statement, and BindRead binds the sequential READ for every edition (NEXT has no effect, §1985:VII.4.4.4 GR2); the later editions' additions are refused at 85 on recognition, each COBOL0900: PREVIOUS (VisitReadDirection), WITH [NO] LOCK, IGNORING LOCK and ADVANCING ON LOCK (VisitRecordLockPhrase, VisitReadIgnoringLock, VisitReadAdvancingOnLock), RETRY (VisitRetryPhrase); KEY IS and INVALID KEY on a sequential file are refused (COBOL2269, COBOL1720), as are READ FILE, a record-name operand, a literal after INTO, a second AT END and an AT END with no statement or with a conditional one. Probed at 85: READ F1, RECORD, NEXT, NEXT RECORD INTO, AT END and END without AT, with and without NOT AT END and END-READ, and a READ nested in an AT END phrase compile and run. Not implemented: the printed sequence of the two phrases. conditionalPhrases is ({conditionalPhraseAssociates($ctx)}? conditionalPhrase)* and Associates / MayAssociate ask only that a phrase is printed by a format of the statement and is not yet written, with no edition arm for the order, so NOT AT END written before AT END compiles and runs at 85. Either order is the 2002 change (§2002:F.2 item 33: the conditional phrases of READ and fifteen other statements "may be specified in any order"), which this row's change record names as what 2023 accepts and 1985 refuses. Same mechanism as the indexed rows 1985-FMT-IX.4.3.2, IX.4.5.2, IX.4.6.2, IX.4.7.2 and IX.4.9.2 of this pass. The witness reads with RECORD INTO and with INTO alone, both phrases in the printed order, END-READ on each.

next.reason: §1985:VII.4.4.2 is 'READ file-name-1 [NEXT] RECORD [INTO identifier-1] [AT END ...] [NOT AT END ...] [END-READ]', AT END before NOT AT END. §2023:14.9.30.2 'Format 1 (sequential)' accepts every such READ with the same meaning, the omitted NEXT given by §2023:14.9.30.3 SR8 ('If neither the NEXT phrase nor the PREVIOUS phrase is specified and ACCESS MODE SEQUENTIAL is specified ... the NEXT phrase is implied'); but it adds PREVIOUS, ADVANCING ON LOCK, IGNORING LOCK, the retry-phrase and WITH [NO] LOCK, and puts AT END and NOT AT END in choice-indicator brackets, so either order is accepted. Programs the 1985 format refuses are accepted, no refusal made an exception condition: CHANGED.
